the rate of dentition changes in children with sagittal bite deviations is slower than normal and that it is characterized by a tendency to a greater extent of dental arch asymmetry.

the rate and localization of age-related dentation changes are determined by the sagittal occlusal position of the jaws.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate and localization of dental changes in children with sagittal bite disorders are different from the norm.
in the early stages of development, the dentition of children with prognathism and prognathism with an open bite is more stable, while children with prognathic bite have more pronounced changes.
